meanings.meaning: 毒药，毒物（指能使生物中毒的有害物质） verb. 下毒，毒害
meanings.usage: 表示投放毒物使中毒的动作
不可数名词，指口腔分泌的消化液
常用于修饰与消化功能相关的器官、液体等
后接名词，表示某事物难以被完成/理解，或公然违抗规则、权威
不可数名词，指被其他动物捕食的生物
可作可数或不可数名词，指非必需的、能带来便利或享受的事物

meanings.meaning: 食肉动物（指以肉类为主要食物的动物，反义词为herbivore（食草动物））
脊椎动物（指有脊椎骨的动物，反义词为invertebrate（无脊椎动物））

meanings.usage: 可指调配物质，也可指编造故事、借口等
不可数名词，指药物、毒物等的作用强度
常与介词of/into搭配，表示从一种形式变为另一种形式的过程
特指生物分泌的有毒液体，区别于普通的poison
用于描述事物发展的初期阶段，相对不够先进
可指化学配方、数学公式，也可指方案、方法

phrases.usage: 表示以某物为食、靠某物生存

examples.en: They could have caught and lived on prey without using poison.
examples.zh: 它们本可以不用毒液，就捕获猎物并以此为生。

examples.en: Most pandas live on bamboo in the wild.
examples.zh: 野外的大多数大熊猫以竹子为食。

phrases.usage: 比喻具有利弊两面性的事物，即双刃剑

examples.en: It would be an assistance to all carnivores though it would be a two-edged weapon when they fought each other.
examples.zh: 这对所有食肉动物都有帮助，不过当它们互相打斗时，这就会是一把双刃剑。

examples.en: Social media is a two-edged weapon: it connects people but also spreads misinformation easily.
examples.zh: 社交媒体是一把双刃剑：它能连接人们，但也很容易传播不实信息。

phrases.usage: 用于形容词或副词比较级、最高级前，强调程度，意为“……得多，显然”

examples.en: Both poisons are unpleasant, but by far the more unpleasant is the blood poison.
examples.zh: 两种毒液都很可怕，但血溶性毒液显然要更伤人。

examples.en: This is by far the best movie I have watched this year.
examples.zh: 这显然是我今年看过的最好的电影。

phrases.usage: 插入语，用于表达比喻、不太严谨的说法，意为“可以说，打个比方”

examples.en: The blood poison is, so to speak, a newer product from an improved formula.
examples.zh: 可以说，血溶性毒液是配方改良后的新产品。

examples.en: In many ways, the Internet is, so to speak, a new global public space.
examples.zh: 从很多方面来说，互联网可以说是一个全新的全球公共空间。

phrases.usage: 让步表达，意为“尽管如此，话虽如此”，用于承认前文观点后转折引出新内容

examples.en: Be that as it may, the nerve poison does its business with man far more quickly than the blood poison.
examples.zh: 尽管如此，神经性毒液作用于人体的速度还是比血溶性毒液快得多。

examples.en: Be that as it may, we still need to consider the potential risks of the plan.
examples.zh: 话虽如此，我们还是需要考虑这个计划的潜在风险。

phrases.usage: 非正式表达，意为“发挥作用，奏效”

examples.en: The nerve poison does its business with man far more quickly than the blood poison.
examples.zh: 神经性毒液对人体产生作用的速度比血溶性毒液快得多。

examples.en: The medicine will do its business in half an hour and you will feel less pain.
examples.zh: 这个药半小时后就会起效，你就不会那么疼了。

grammar.title: 虚拟语气：could have done
grammar.structure: 主语 + could have + 动词过去分词
grammar.definition: 表示对过去本可以发生但实际没有发生的事情的假设，译为“本可以做某事（却没做）” 用于评论过去的行为，表达遗憾、推测或者假设的可能性

examples.en: They could have caught and lived on prey without using poison, just as the thousands of non-poisonous snakes still do.
examples.zh: 它们本可以不用毒液，就捕获猎物并以此为生，就像数千种无毒蛇现在仍然做的那样。

examples.en: You could have passed the exam if you had studied harder last week.
examples.zh: 如果你上周更努力学习的话，你本可以通过考试的。

grammar.title: 定语从句的省略形式
grammar.structure: 先行词 + （关系代词 + be动词） + 分词/形容词/介词短语
grammar.definition: 当定语从句的主语与先行词一致，且从句谓语包含be动词时，可以省略关系代词和be动词，保留其余成分 用于简化句子结构，使表达更简洁，常见于书面语

examples.en: Over the periods their saliva, a mild, digestive juice like our own, was converted into a poison that defies analysis even today.
examples.zh: 经过很长的时间，它们的唾液——一种和我们的唾液一样的温和消化液——转变成了一种甚至至今都无法分析清楚的毒液。

examples.en: The book written by my favorite author has sold over 1 million copies.
examples.zh: 我最喜欢的作家写的那本书已经卖出了超过100万册。

patterns.pattern: How it came about that... is a mystery.

original.en: How it came about that snakes manufactured poison is a mystery.
original.zh: 蛇是如何产生毒液的，这是个谜。

imitations.en: How it came about that this ancient building survived the war is a mystery.
imitations.zh: 这座古建筑是如何在战争中幸存下来的，这是个谜。

imitations.en: How it came about that he mastered three foreign languages in two years is a mystery to all of us.
imitations.zh: 他是如何在两年内掌握三门外语的，对我们所有人来说都是个谜。

original.en: It is said that the nerve poison is the more primitive of the two, that the blood poison is, so to speak, a newer product from an improved formula.
original.zh: 据说在这两种毒液中，神经性毒液是更原始的一种，可以说，血溶性毒液是配方改良后的新产品。

imitations.en: It is said that this place used to be a royal garden, that many emperors spent their summers here.
imitations.zh: 据说这个地方曾经是皇家园林，很多皇帝都在这里避暑。

imitations.en: It is said that drinking warm water in the morning is good for your stomach, that it helps speed up your metabolism.
imitations.zh: 据说早上喝温水对胃有好处，还能帮助加快新陈代谢。

patterns.pattern: ...did not acquire... for use against... but for use against...

original.en: Snakes did not acquire their poison for use against man but for use against prey such as rats and mice.
original.zh: 蛇获得毒液不是为了用来对抗人类，而是为了用来对付老鼠之类的猎物。

imitations.en: He did not take the course for use against exams but for use against practical problems in his work.
imitations.zh: 他学这门课不是为了应付考试，而是为了解决工作中的实际问题。

imitations.en: This law was not made for use against ordinary citizens but for use against people who break public order.
imitations.zh: 这项法律的制定不是为了约束普通公民，而是为了惩治破坏公共秩序的人。

translation:
蛇是怎样产生毒液的，这是一个谜。蛇的唾液本来和我们人的消化液一样柔和，但经过漫长的时间，演变成了今天仍无法分析清楚的毒液。毒液不是生存竞争强加给它们的，它们也可以不用毒液捕捉动物而生存，就像今天成千上万的无毒蛇那样。毒液对毒蛇来说只不过是一种舒适生存的优越手段，它使蛇不用费多大力气就能捕获到食物，轻咬一口即可。为什么只有蛇才有毒液呢？譬如说，如果猫有毒液，那对猫会大有帮助，它就不必再和又大又凶的老鼠边跑边博斗了，也不必再和大兔子扭斗了，只要咬一口，就不必再费大力气。因此，任何食肉动物有了毒液，都能从中获益。不过，当它们相互撕打时，毒液就成了利弊参半的武，可以杀死对方，也可以被对方的毒液杀死。然而，在脊椎动物中，大自然神秘模测地只选择了蛇（还有一种蜥蜴），人们弄不清楚大自然为什么在某些蛇的身上调制出如此高效的毒液来。
人们可能认为，唾液转变成毒液，其中有固定的程序。其实没有。有些蛇产生的毒液也在各方面与另外一些毒蛇产生的毒液不同，就像砒霜不同于马钱子碱一样。不同毒蛇产生的毒液产生的效果不同，一种毒液作用于神经，另一种毒液作用于血液。
产生神经毒液的蛇有一种非洲树眼镜蛇和眼镜蛇，它们的毒液称为神经毒素。蝰蛇（蝮蛇）和响尾蛇产生血液毒素，称为溶血性毒液。这两种毒液都很可怕，但溶血性毒液尤其厉害。据说，神经毒液在两种毒液中是较为原始的一种，而溶血性毒液，打个比方说，是根据改良配方生产的一种较新的产品。不过，神经毒辣液比溶血性毒液在人身上起作用快得多。但是，这没有什么关系，因为蛇有毒液不是用来对付人的，而是对付它的猎物，诸如鼠类，毒液对这些猎物会立刻起作用。

lines.en: How it came about that snakes manufactured poison is a mystery.
Over the periods their saliva , a mild, digestive juice like our own, was converted into a poison that defies analysis even today.
It was not forced upon them by the survival competition; they could have caught and lived on prey without using poison, just as the thousands of non-poisonous snakes still do.
Poison to a snake is merely a luxury; it enables it to get its food with very little effort, no more effort than one bite.
And why only snakes?
Cats, for instance, would be greatly helped; no running fights with large, fierce rats or tussles with grown rabbits -- just a bite and no more effort needed.
In fact, it would be an assistance to all carnivores though it would be a two-edged weapon when they fought each other.
But, of the vertebrates, unpredictable Nature selected only snakes (and one lizard ).
One wonders saliva into why Nature, with respect from that of others, as other on the blood.
In the conversion of saliva into poison, one might suppose that a fixed process took place.
It did not; some snakes manufacture a poison different in every respect from that of others, as different as arsenic is from strychnine, and having different effects.
One poison acts on the nerves, the other on the blood.
The makers of the nerve poison include the mambas and the cobras and their venom is called neurotoxic.
Vipers (adders) and rattlesnakes manufacture the blood poison, which is known as haemolytic.
Both poisons are unpleasant, but by far the more unpleasant is the blood poison.
It is said that the nerve poison is the more primitive of the two, that the blood poison is, so to speak, a newer product from an improved formula.
Be that as it may, the nerve poison does its business with man far more quickly than the blood poison.
This, however, means nothing.
Snakes did not acquire their poison for use against man but for use against prey such as rats and mice, and the effects on these of viperine poison is almost immediate .
JOHN CROMPTON The snake

lead.summary: 蛇是怎样产生毒液的，这是一个谜。蛇的唾液本来和我们人的消化液一样柔和，但经过漫长的时间，演变成了今天仍无法分析清楚的毒液。
